How Stanislav Petrov’s single, agonizing decision to trust his gut over his computer screens prevented a Soviet retaliatory nuclear strike during a 1983 false alarm.
The harrowing escape of Belgian King Albert I’s secret courier, who swam the freezing Yser River under German searchlights to deliver the flood orders that saved the last slice of Belgium in 1914.
The extreme, claustrophobic reality of a German U-boat cook during WWII, managing a tiny, grease-slicked galley while depth charges rattled the hull and oxygen slowly ran out.

The high-stakes gamble of Spanish double agent Juan Pujol García (Garbo), who had to invent a fake network of 27 sub-agents and convince the Nazi high command that the D-Day landings were a mere diversion.

The tragic mistake of British Admiral Archibald Berkeley Milne, whose hesitation and misread signals allowed the German battlecruiser SMS Goeben to escape to Constantinople, ultimately dragging the Ottoman Empire into WWI.

The 15-minute window of Captain Charles McVay: How a single naval officer was court-martialed by his own government to cover up the systemic failure that left the crew of the torpedoed USS Indianapolis to be eaten alive by sharks in the Philippine Sea.

The claustrophobic nightmare of Corporal Hiroo Onoda’s final night in the jungle: A vivid look at the psychological breaking point of the Japanese holdout who spent 29 years waging a solo guerrilla war in the Philippine jungle, refusing to believe WWII had ended.

The desperate, secret flight of Princess Mafalda of Savoy: How the daughter of the Italian King was lured into a trap by the Gestapo on the pretext of a phone call from her missing husband, ending in her tragic imprisonment in Buchenwald.

The agonizing gamble of Dr. Eugene Lazowski: The Polish doctor who created a fake typhus epidemic by injecting thousands of villagers with a harmless dead bacterium, risking execution by the Gestapo to save entire towns from being sent to concentration camps.

The fatal hesitation of General Charles de Lanrezac: The French commander who defied his own Supreme Commander's suicidal offensive doctrine at the Battle of Charleroi in 1914, risking his career and being branded a coward to save the entire French Army from annihilation.

The 18-year-old French farm girl who accidentally started WWI: The panicked moment Marie-Jeanne Gabert sprinted down a country road shouting warnings about a burning farmhouse, triggering the mobilization orders that set Europe on fire.

The death of General George S. Patton in a mundane traffic accident: How a freak low-speed collision in post-war Germany robbed the Allies of their most volatile, prophetic commander just as the Cold War's iron curtain was descending.

The decoy army made of rubber and inflatable tanks: The surreal, high-stakes game of deception where a troupe of Hollywood set designers and sound engineers fooled the Luftwaffe into looking at a ghost army before D-Day.

The catastrophic miscalculation of Admiral Sir George Tryon: The bizarre peacetime maneuver off the coast of Tripoli where a legendary Royal Navy commander stubbornly ordered two massive battleships to turn directly into each other, watched in horror by hundreds of sailors on deck.

The frozen inkwell of Captain Robert Falcon Scott: The final, agonizing diary entries written inside a blizzard-swept tent in Antarctica as his dying expedition realized they were beaten to the South Pole by just 34 days.

The painter who forged Hitler\'s signature to save thousands: How a Dutch art forger in occupied Amsterdam faked Nazi transit papers so convincingly that the Gestapo used his forgeries to route French resistance fighters to safety.

The rogue submarine commander who accidentally started the Pacific War: How Dutch Lieutenant Commander A.A. Mulder sank a Japanese ship off Malaya hours *before* Pearl Harbor, forcing Tokyo\'s hand and altering the global timeline of WWII.

The forgotten ride of Sofija Jovanović, the 17-year-old Serbian volunteer who picked up the discarded rifle of a fallen officer during the 1912 artillery barrage of the First Balkan War and went on to fight in the trenches of WWI disguised as a male soldier.

The fateful dinner party of Gavrilo Princip: The astonishingly mundane moment in a Sarajevo cafe where the assassin sat eating a sandwich just minutes after his initial plot failed, only for Archduke Franz Ferdinand's driver to take a wrong turn right outside the window.

The accidental courier of Pearl Harbor: How a 22-year-old US Army private named Joseph Lockard watched a massive swarm of unknown planes on an untested radar screen on the morning of December 7, 1941, only to have his frantic warning dismissed by a rookie lieutenant as incoming B-17 bombers from California.

How General George S. Patton’s sudden death in a mundane 1945 car crash left his chief of staff, Major General Hobart Gay, scrambling to secure Patton’s controversial, anti-Soviet diaries before military censors could confiscate them.

How a single, mistranslated diplomatic cable in Berlin on August 1, 1914, tricked Kaiser Wilhelm II into halting the German army's advance against France, creating a frantic 90-minute window where World War I nearly didn't happen as ordered.

How a lone British radar operator on the cliffs of Dover ignored a phantom blip on his glowing cathode-ray tube on the morning of May 10, 1941, nearly missing Rudolf Hess’s unauthorized Messerschmitt crash-landing in Scotland.
